_comment: A routed squadron caught on its flank by spearmen gets clear of them (#1913, re-judged for #1949). A brittle player squadron (20 Cavalry at morale 0.4) stands facing west; an enemy Spearmen block (48 men, 12 files) 240 wu to its south, facing it, marches up onto its left flank with no player input. The squadron is in contact from about tick 637 and routs at tick 676 still in contact (the setup checks: IDLE at 674, ROUTING and in contact at 676). Each routed man then runs on his own from the spearmen he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), and the spearmen follow in their ranks at the edge of their reach. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-13 on #1949's branch: the squadron is still in the spearmen's reach at tick 760, out of it at tick 800 on seeds 1, 3 and 4, and still at the edge of it then on seeds 0 and 2, which the spearmen follow closely. So the clip pins the flight itself: its men's centroid runs north from (899.98, 691.09) at the rout to (882.46 to 929.39, 630.79 to 647.03) at tick 800, pinned at the span's midpoint (905.9, 638.9) with a tol of 24 wu reaching its farther ends; a rout stalled in the spearmen's reach would read about (900, 690), outside it. The out-of-contact pin at tick 800, which seeds 0 and 2 now fail, is retired for it. #1913 pinned the squadron's couple() anchor at ticks 705, 708, 732 and 735 ((917.74, 686.78) to (920.96, 678.28), tol 5.9 wu) to guard against that anchor switching back and forth between the front ranks and the whole block at the edge of the spearmen's reach. The bottom-up flight (#1949) removed the anchor: a routed unit's position is the centroid of its men. So those four pins are retired, and the tick-800 centroid pin carries the clip's claim. The squadron is still routing when the clip ends at tick 800.
